title: Lauda Air 004
summary: Lauda Air Flight 004, a Boeing 767-300ER flying from Hong Kong via Bangkok to Vienna, crashed into mountainous jungle terrain in Thailand on 26 May 1991 after the thrust reverser on the No. 1 engine deployed uncommanded during the climb. The pilots had received an EICAS advisory about a possible reverser fault nine minutes earlier but took no remedial action, believing it a false indication. The reverser deployment disrupted airflow over the wing, causing a 25% loss of lift and an aerodynamic stall; the aircraft entered a diving left turn and in-flight breakup, killing all 223 people on board.
probable_cause: Thailand's Aircraft Accident Investigation Committee determined the probable cause to be an uncommanded in-flight deployment of the left engine thrust reverser, which resulted in loss of flight path control; the specific cause of the deployment was not positively identified.

factors.evidence: The No. 1 engine reverser deployed while the plane was over mountainous jungle terrain, and Thurner's last recorded words were 'Oh, reverser's deployed.'
After consulting the aircraft's Quick Reference Handbook, they determined that the alert was 'coming on and off' and that it was 'just an advisory thing.'
The accident report states that the 'flight crew training simulators yielded erroneous results' and that recovery from the loss of lift 'was uncontrollable for an unexpecting flight crew.'
An aerodynamic plume of air disrupted the airflow over the leading edge of the left wing during the engine's rundown to idle thrust, which resulted in a 25% loss of lift and an aerodynamic stall.
The aircraft immediately began a diving left turn, resulting in an uncontrolled dive and in-flight breakup.

events.text: At 23:08, Welch and Thurner received a visual warning indication on the EICAS display that a possible system failure would cause the thrust reverser on the No. 1 engine to deploy in flight.
After consulting the Quick Reference Handbook, the pilots determined the alert was 'coming on and off' and 'just an advisory thing' and took no remedial action.
At 23:17, the No. 1 engine reverser deployed while the plane was over mountainous jungle terrain, and Thurner's last recorded words were 'Oh, reverser's deployed.'
An aerodynamic plume of air disrupted the airflow over the leading edge of the left wing, causing a 25% loss of lift and an aerodynamic stall, and the aircraft immediately began a diving left turn.
The aircraft suffered an uncontrolled dive and in-flight breakup, killing all 213 passengers and ten crew members on board.

title: Nigeria Airways 2120
summary: Nigeria Airways Flight 2120 caught fire shortly after takeoff from Jeddah on July 11, 1991, when underinflated tires overheated and burst on the runway. The crew was unaware of the fire in the wheel assembly area and attempted to return for an emergency landing, but lost flight control capability as the fire consumed hydraulic and electrical systems. The aircraft crashed while attempting to return, killing all 261 people on board.
probable_cause: Takeoff was attempted with underinflated tires that overheated, burst, and ignited during the takeoff roll. The fire in the landing gear area consumed hydraulic and electrical systems, causing loss of control. A project manager had prevented tire replacement despite maintenance notification to meet the flight schedule.

factors.evidence: Burning rubber from overheated tires was brought into close proximity with hydraulic and electrical system components when landing gear was retracted.

The lead mechanic noticed that the No. 2 and No. 4 tyre pressures were below minimum for flight dispatch and attempted to inflate them, but the project manager dismissed the problem and readied the aircraft for dispatch.
Hydraulic systems failed as the fire from burning tires destroyed hydraulic lines.
The aircraft took off with landing gear in unsafe condition with underinflated tires.
The project manager, unwilling to accept a delay, dismissed the maintenance concern and readied the aircraft for dispatch.

events.text: Lead mechanic noticed No. 2 and No. 4 tire pressures were below minimum for flight dispatch and attempted to inflate them.
Project manager dismissed the tire pressure problem and readied the aircraft for dispatch.
No. 1 tire failed very early on takeoff roll, followed by No. 2 tire stopping rotation; friction generated sufficient heat to start self-sustaining fire.
First Officer Davidge reported losing hydraulics and requested return to airport for emergency landing.
In-flight director reported smoke in the back to the cockpit.
First Officer Davidge reported losing ailerons, forcing Captain Allan to take manual control.

title: Indian Airlines 257
summary: Indian Airlines Flight 257 crashed into Thangjing Hill during descent on approach to Imphal. The pilot deliberately violated the published approach procedure by flying direct to Imphal instead of via Agartala, changed heading to 053 degrees from the planned 007 degrees, and reported a false position to ATC while failing to monitor instruments.
probable_cause: Pilot's deliberate non-adherence to published approach procedure; over-reliance on terrain familiarity; inadequate instrument monitoring; loss of situational awareness.

factors.evidence: The crew decided to violate the approach procedure by taking a short cut
The crew reported that they were above the supposed VOR but they were nowhere near the said location
During the approach, the crew did not adequately monitor their instruments, despite the deteriorating weather condition
Flight 257 began to deviate to heading 053, significantly off to the right from its supposed heading of 007
the aircraft crashed into the hilly terrain of Thangjing Hill during its descent

events.text: Flight 257 took off at 11:54 from Calcutta bound for Imphal.
After contacting Chittagong's Comilla Airport and Tripura's Agartala, the crew was asked to contact Imphal Tower for descent clearance.
Flight 257 began to deviate to heading 053, significantly off to the right from its supposed heading of 007.
The crew reported that they were above the supposed VOR, but they were nowhere near the said location.
ATC later warned the crew that there was rain on the eastern area of the airport.
Imphal Airport lost contact with the aircraft just after 12:45, at 1500 m altitude.
